video_title: Cavs vs Timberwolves | Donovan Mitchell Media Availability | 10.26.2026

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on Emoni Bates' impressive rookie debut
quotes.excerpt: It's very rare to ride the coattails of a rookie going into a half.
quotes.quote: It's very rare to ride the coattails of a rookie going into a half. We didn't have energy, we were flat, we were playing the wrong way, we weren't doing the right things. And for him to be the spark in his first game of the year, that's not normal. That speaks to him, his preparation, his confidence, his concentration, attention to detail. He made some mistakes, but they were aggressive mistakes. He went to go for a steal, got out of position, but you live with those rather than being passive. He made the most out of his moment. I didn't even know he had 16 points, but 16 points, fearless, just trying to find ways to impact the game at the highest level. I told him the best part of his game wasn't even the 16 points, it was the energy.
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell praised rookie Emoni Bates for providing a much needed spark off the bench. Mitchell said it is rare to ride the coattails of a rookie but Bates was fearless and brought the energy the team lacked in the first half.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell discusses the impact of rookie Emoni Bates during his debut game.

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell praises Emoni Bates' defensive attention to detail
quotes.excerpt: His attention to detail defensively, I think was the biggest thing.
quotes.quote: His attention to detail defensively, I think was the biggest thing. Offensively, he makes shots, he's a killer. That doesn't surprise me. But the fact that he's trying and willing and trying to learn, he texts me all the time saying, 'What about this clip? Why did you go rotate here? Why did I do this? Should I have done this?' Today, this morning, he was working on shows. What rookie is working on shows? They're usually working on, 'How I get to the corner for a three?' He's working on trying to impact the ball defensively. That to me was what really stood out, and when you're worried about the right stuff, good things usually follow.
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell says he is impressed by Emoni Bates' defensive work ethic. Mitchell noted that while most rookies focus on scoring, Bates is actively studying film and working on defensive rotations to impact the game.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell praises the defensive work ethic and attention to detail shown by Emoni Bates.

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on the importance of role players like Emoni Bates
quotes.excerpt: I don't get to do what I do, Jarrett doesn't get to that, Evan doesn't get to those big shots without Malik.
quotes.quote: It's really not about me and Jarrett. I feel like we did what we do, but at the end of the day, we don't get there. I don't get to do what I do, Jarrett doesn't get to that, Evan doesn't get to those big shots without Emoni Bates giving the energy in the first half. Even Payton Watson. At the end of the day, our job is to do what you, as we did tonight, but it's the other guys, it's the role guys. Somebody's stepping up for us to be able to be at that level. So that's to me is like, that's why. At the end of the day, yeah, Jarrett and I went back and forth and Evan hit some big threes and what not, but at the end of the day, we don't get to that position.
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell emphasized that the Cavs' success depends on role players stepping up. Mitchell credited Emoni Bates for providing the energy necessary to put the team in a position to win, regardless of his own scoring output.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell explains the importance of role players like Emoni Bates and Payton Watson to the team's success.

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on Payton Watson's defensive impact
quotes.excerpt: Payton's a tough cover, and it's easy for when a guy's got it rolling to get discouraged.
quotes.quote: Payton's a tough cover, and it's easy for when a guy's got it rolling to get discouraged. But for him, especially the last shot, for Payton to get downhill, for him to recover and block it, he had another one where he's blocking it. Those plays go a long way for us, him being in the gaps, him being on the boards, and just making it tough. At the end of the day, Payton is Payton. He's going to have nights like this, but making it tough on them, and that's what Payton did all night. We ended up getting the stops we needed most, and that's truly all that matters.
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell highlighted the defensive impact of Payton Watson, specifically praising his ability to recover and make key blocks. Mitchell noted that Watson's effort in the gaps and on the boards was crucial to getting the stops they needed.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell highlights the defensive contributions and hustle plays made by Payton Watson.

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on why playing with a big lead is difficult
quotes.excerpt: Because of the pace and the three-point shooting and like, it's just so different now.
quotes.quote: Because of the pace and the three-point shooting and like, it's just so different now. This is going to sound insane when I say this to myself, but when I first got into the league, I don't like thinking that I'm that old, but when I first got into the league, a 20-point lead was like, that's ballgame. Even before I got into the league. But there's so many more possessions, there's so the guys are picking up full court, there's like there's so many. It's random basketball. Even look at the Toronto series, they're randomly doubling at half. That's AAU basketball. And it's not bad, it's just the way the game has gone now.
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell reflects on how the NBA has changed, noting that a 20 point lead is no longer safe. Mitchell says the increase in possessions and random defensive schemes like full court pressure make modern games feel like AAU basketball.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell reflects on how the pace and style of the modern NBA make large leads less secure than in the past.

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on the psychological aspect of maintaining leads
quotes.excerpt: I think a lot of that is is being intentional.
quotes.quote: I think a lot of that is is being intentional. If we go look at, I'm going to throw a game out here, the the Spurs in the finals, right? The offense was a little different when they were up versus when they how they got the lead. And naturally, because sometimes you play to protect the lead. The Argentina game that he showed, one of the players said that we were playing not to lose as opposed to playing to win. It happens across all sports. I think now, to your point, there is a psychological piece to it and it's like, all right, what are we going to do in these two-minute spurts? If they give up an old board, are we not letting it happen again? If we turn it over, are we not doing that again? Are we not compounding mistakes? That's truly what it is.
quotes.social_post: Donovan Mitchell discusses the psychological challenge of maintaining leads. He explains that teams often fall into the trap of playing not to lose, and emphasizes the need to be intentional about not compounding mistakes during two minute spurts.

structured.context: Donovan Mitchell discusses the psychological challenge of maintaining leads and avoiding compounding mistakes during games.
